page: Amazon Web Services m7gd.2xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by an 8-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 ARM64 processor running at 2.6 GHz. It features 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per dedicated physical core. The instance is built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and includes 474 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage, alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate solid general-purpose performance, with average scores across Geekbench single-core and multi-core tests, as well as software compilation and image processing workloads. Passmark memory tests show strong performance, placing in the top 25%, which aligns with the high-speed memory architecture of the Graviton platform. However, the instance exhibits weaker performance in specific compute-heavy tasks, such as bzip3 decompression and Passmark CPU encryption tests, which fell into the bottom 10% and 25% respectively. LLM inference benchmarks also show limitations, particularly for prompt processing on medium-sized models.

The inclusion of local NVMe SSD storage directly on the instance provides a cost-efficient alternative to attaching external block storage for applications requiring low-latency scratch space. Given its balanced resource allocation and local storage, the m7gd.2xlarge is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, local database caching, static web serving, and application development environments that benefit from ARM64 architecture and high memory bandwidth.
description: Amazon Web Services m7gd.2xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 8 dedicated ARM64 cores powered by an AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 processor running at 2.6 GHz. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of memory and 474 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage, operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps. Performance benchmarks show average results for general compute, software compilation, and web serving, with strong memory performance in Passmark tests. However, it exhibits weaker performance in bzip3 decompression and cryptographic operations. The integrated local NVMe storage offers qualitative cost efficiency by eliminating the need for external block storage for temporary data. This instance is suited for general-purpose applications, static web serving, and database workloads requiring high-speed local scratch space.
